sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *según* + the source and *decir que* from B1 Unit 13. After a past verb such as *dijo*, the verb inside moves back: *hay* becomes *había*, *hemos cometido* becomes *habían cometido*. When two sides disagree about the same events, each statement gets its own source. That keeps your voice out of it: you say who said what.

sections.title: Who said what
rows: Según la ONU, murieron más de trescientas personas.
source first: According to the UN, more than three hundred people died.
Los expertos dijeron que había violaciones graves.
dijo que + imperfect: The experts said there were serious violations.
El gobierno dijo que las protestas eran un intento de golpe de Estado.
the other side, with its own source
Según el gobierno, la protesta fue ilegal.

items.spanish: Según la Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos, murieron más de trescientas personas en las protestas de 2018.
items.english: According to the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, more than three hundred people died in the 2018 protests.

items.spanish: Expertos de la ONU dijeron que el gobierno había cometido graves violaciones de derechos humanos.
items.english: UN experts said that the government had committed serious human rights violations.

items.spanish: El gobierno dijo que las protestas eran un intento de golpe de Estado.
items.english: The government said that the protests were an attempt at a coup.

items.spanish: Según Sergio Ramírez, los escritores en el exilio siguen escribiendo sobre Nicaragua.
items.english: According to Sergio Ramírez, writers in exile keep writing about Nicaragua.

sections.content: After *decir* there is no *de*: *dijeron que había*, not *dijeron de que había*. With *según* you do not need *que*. Always give each side its own source, and put no opinion of your own in the sentence.
